notes: The official ArcGIS feature service is public, paginable, and point-geocoded.
Denver's crime-information page states that the public surface is NIBRS-based and includes all victims of person crimes and all crimes within an incident.
The 2024 row set is effectively fully geocoded: only one record lacks direct lat/lon, and that record still has an incident address.
The service exposes a public NIBRS sex-related vocabulary, but no repo-compatible rape bucket exists on the public surface.
The public ontology appears much closer to NIBRS than to legacy UCR Part I.
The main packet risk is not missing geocodes; it is comparability between Denver's NIBRS-coded incident/victim surface and the public dashboard/archive offense totals used as anchors.
Person-crime totals should be reconciled on VICTIM_COUNT; property crimes reconcile on row count.
Denver also publishes theft-from-motor-vehicle as a separate category, but the repo surface keeps it out of the seven-offense city-share model.

sources: Denver Crime Information page overall crime dashboard
Denver Crime Statistics Archive references on the same official page
notes: The city exposes official public crime dashboards and archive links on the police crime-information page.
The packet now has an explicit 2024 offense-by-offense extraction and reconciliation artifact.
The crime-information page says the dashboard has year-to-date, 28-day, 180-day, and complete past-year views.

why_not_ready: The public source is strong enough to onboard offense-selectively, but rape remains blocked because Denver has no repo-compatible rape bucket.
The public surface is NIBRS incident/victim oriented, so person-crime counts require victim-count reconciliation instead of a pure incident count.
minimum_change_to_unblock: No further change is needed for the current offense-selective release.
If the repo ever adds a Denver-compatible sexual-assault bucket, revisit the blocked rape mapping.
